quests.hint: A preposition that shows two people are different.
quests.explanation: 'Unlike' + noun compares by contrast: 'Unlike her brother, she is modest.' Its opposite 'like' shows similarity.
quests.textToSpeak: She's very modest, ___ her brother, who never stops boasting about his achievements.
quests.correctAnswer: She's very modest, unlike her brother, who never stops boasting about his achievements.
quests.contextClue: The two siblings are contrasted.

quests.hint: It means 'without being affected by'.
quests.explanation: 'Regardless of' + noun means despite; the conditions don't matter: 'regardless of the weather'.
quests.textToSpeak: The match will go ahead ___ of the weather, so bring waterproofs just in case.
quests.correctAnswer: The match will go ahead regardless of the weather, so bring waterproofs just in case.
quests.contextClue: The plan does not change with the weather, yet waterproofs are advised.

quests.hint: A word that leaves the amount of effort open.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever it takes' means do everything necessary. 'Whatever' can also mean 'anything that': 'Do whatever you like'.
quests.textToSpeak: You have to finish the project on time, ___ it takes, even if that means working weekends.
quests.correctAnswer: You have to finish the project on time, whatever it takes, even if that means working weekends.
quests.contextClue: Working weekends is an example of the effort.

quests.hint: At any time that.
quests.explanation: 'Whenever' means every time or at any time that. It is written as one word.
quests.textToSpeak: Call me ___ you need help, day or night; I'm a light sleeper.
quests.correctAnswer: Call me whenever you need help, day or night; I'm a light sleeper.
quests.contextClue: 'Day or night' means any moment.

quests.hint: In any place that.
quests.explanation: 'Wherever' means in any place that: 'wherever you go'. It is written as one word.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll follow you ___ you go, as long as we stay together.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll follow you wherever you go, as long as we stay together.
quests.contextClue: Staying together matters more than the place.

quests.hint: A word that introduces the specific item you have just referred to.
quests.explanation: 'Namely' introduces the specific detail you are about to name: 'one thing matters, namely trust'.
quests.textToSpeak: Only one thing matters in this negotiation, ___ trust; without it, nothing else works.
quests.correctAnswer: Only one thing matters in this negotiation, namely trust; without it, nothing else works.
quests.contextClue: The general 'one thing' is then named.

quests.hint: Be greater in importance than something else.
quests.explanation: 'Outweigh' means be more important than: 'the benefits outweigh the risks'.
quests.textToSpeak: Moving abroad will be difficult, but in the end I think the benefits will ___ the drawbacks.
quests.correctAnswer: Moving abroad will be difficult, but in the end I think the benefits will outweigh the drawbacks.
quests.contextClue: Benefits and drawbacks are being compared.

quests.hint: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
quests.explanation: 'Inevitable' means certain to happen. The adverb is 'inevitably'.
quests.textToSpeak: With the company expanding so fast, a few mistakes were ___.
quests.correctAnswer: With the company expanding so fast, a few mistakes were inevitable.
quests.contextClue: Fast expansion leads to errors that cannot be avoided.

quests.hint: Demand firmly that something happens.
quests.explanation: 'Insist on' + -ing or noun means firmly demand: 'insist on paying'. It is used to refuse a polite protest.
quests.textToSpeak: I ___ on paying for dinner tonight; you paid last time, and I won't take no for an answer.
quests.correctAnswer: I insist on paying for dinner tonight; you paid last time, and I won't take no for an answer.
quests.contextClue: 'Won't take no for an answer' shows firmness.

quests.hint: Fail to notice or consider.
quests.explanation: 'Overlook' means fail to see or consider something: 'overlook a detail'. It can also mean have a view over: 'overlooks the sea'.
quests.textToSpeak: It's easy to ___ small details when you are rushing to meet a deadline.
quests.correctAnswer: It's easy to overlook small details when you are rushing to meet a deadline.
quests.contextClue: Rushing reduces attention to detail.

quests.hint: Think something is smaller or easier than it really is.
quests.explanation: 'Underestimate' means judge something to be less than it is. The opposite is 'overestimate'.
quests.textToSpeak: Never ___ how long a simple repair can take once you actually start.
quests.correctAnswer: Never underestimate how long a simple repair can take once you actually start.
quests.contextClue: 'How long... once you start' warns against optimism.

quests.hint: Make someone believe something is true.
quests.explanation: 'Convince someone that...' means make them believe. 'Persuade someone to...' is about getting them to act.
quests.textToSpeak: It took hours to ___ her that the plan was safe, but she finally agreed.
quests.correctAnswer: It took hours to convince her that the plan was safe, but she finally agreed.
quests.contextClue: Belief in safety is the goal.

quests.hint: Feel bitter about something unfair.
quests.explanation: 'Resent' means feel angry or bitter about something you think is unfair. It can be followed by a noun or -ing.
quests.textToSpeak: She began to ___ her brother because he always got the credit for work they did together.
quests.correctAnswer: She began to resent her brother because he always got the credit for work they did together.
quests.contextClue: Unequal credit explains the feeling.

quests.hint: Causing strong disagreement.
quests.explanation: 'Controversial' describes topics that people argue about. The noun is 'controversy'.
quests.textToSpeak: The new tax is highly ___; some people love it, and others hate it.
quests.correctAnswer: The new tax is highly controversial; some people love it, and others hate it.
quests.contextClue: Love and hate show a divided opinion.

quests.hint: Giving a false impression.
quests.explanation: 'Misleading' describes information that gives a false impression, though it may not be an outright lie. The verb is 'mislead'.
quests.textToSpeak: The advertisement was ___: it promised free delivery, but customers were charged for shipping.
quests.correctAnswer: The advertisement was misleading: it promised free delivery, but customers were charged for shipping.
quests.contextClue: A promise contradicted by charges.

quests.hint: Two events happening together by chance.
quests.explanation: A 'coincidence' is two things happening at the same time by chance. The adjective is 'coincidental'.
quests.textToSpeak: Meeting her at the airport was pure ___; neither of us knew the other was travelling.
quests.correctAnswer: Meeting her at the airport was pure coincidence; neither of us knew the other was travelling.
quests.contextClue: Neither person planned it.

quests.hint: Easily harmed or attacked.
quests.explanation: 'Vulnerable to' + noun means easily harmed by something: 'vulnerable to infection'.
quests.textToSpeak: Elderly people who live alone can be especially ___ to scams.
quests.correctAnswer: Elderly people who live alone can be especially vulnerable to scams.
quests.contextClue: Scams target people who are easily harmed.

quests.hint: An adverb that shows doubt about what people say.
quests.explanation: 'Supposedly' reports what people say while showing you doubt it.
quests.textToSpeak: The restaurant is ___ the best in town, but our meal was disappointing.
quests.correctAnswer: The restaurant is supposedly the best in town, but our meal was disappointing.
quests.contextClue: 'But' shows reality did not match the reputation.

quests.hint: An adverb meaning without wanting to.
quests.explanation: 'Reluctantly' means unwillingly. The adjective is 'reluctant': 'reluctant to help'.
quests.textToSpeak: She ___ agreed to help, although she had plenty of her own work to finish.
quests.correctAnswer: She reluctantly agreed to help, although she had plenty of her own work to finish.
quests.contextClue: Her own workload explains her unwillingness.

quests.hint: At the beginning.
quests.explanation: 'Initially' means at the start. It often appears before a contrast with what happened later.
quests.textToSpeak: The company was ___ unwilling to change, but within a year everyone had accepted the new system.
quests.correctAnswer: The company was initially unwilling to change, but within a year everyone had accepted the new system.
quests.contextClue: 'But within a year' contrasts with the start.

quests.hint: Doubtful that something is true.
quests.explanation: 'Sceptical' (British) or 'skeptical' (American) means doubting a claim.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm ___ about the claim that these pills work after just one day.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm sceptical about the claim that these pills work after just one day.
quests.contextClue: One day seems too fast to believe.

quests.hint: Manage to deal with a difficult situation.
quests.explanation: 'Cope with' + noun means manage a difficult situation: 'cope with stress'.
quests.textToSpeak: How do you ___ with so much pressure at work and still find time for your family?
quests.correctAnswer: How do you cope with so much pressure at work and still find time for your family?
quests.contextClue: Pressure and family both require managing.

quests.hint: Give something to make up for a loss.
quests.explanation: 'Compensate someone for' + problem means give something to make up for it.
quests.textToSpeak: The airline agreed to ___ passengers for the long delay with vouchers and free meals.
quests.correctAnswer: The airline agreed to compensate passengers for the long delay with vouchers and free meals.
quests.contextClue: Vouchers and free meals repay the inconvenience.

quests.hint: Pay back money someone spent.
quests.explanation: 'Reimburse someone for' + cost means pay back money they spent. It is formal; 'pay you back' is casual.
quests.textToSpeak: Keep your receipts, and the company will ___ you for any travel costs.
quests.correctAnswer: Keep your receipts, and the company will reimburse you for any travel costs.
quests.contextClue: Receipts prove the money that was spent.

quests.hint: Take something back so it no longer counts.
quests.explanation: 'Withdraw' means remove or take back: 'withdraw an application', 'withdraw money'.
quests.textToSpeak: She decided to ___ her application after she received a better offer from another company.
quests.correctAnswer: She decided to withdraw her application after she received a better offer from another company.
quests.contextClue: A better offer changes the plan.

quests.hint: Take something for granted without checking.
quests.explanation: 'Assume that' means think something is true without proof. The noun is 'assumption'.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't ___ that everyone knows the rules; explain them clearly at the start.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't assume that everyone knows the rules; explain them clearly at the start.
quests.contextClue: Explaining clearly avoids relying on guesses.

quests.hint: Very intense and aggressive.
quests.explanation: 'Fierce competition' is a strong collocation for intense rivalry. Others: 'fierce debate', 'fierce loyalty'.
quests.textToSpeak: There was ___ competition for the job; over two hundred people applied for one position.
quests.correctAnswer: There was fierce competition for the job; over two hundred people applied for one position.
quests.contextClue: Two hundred applicants for one job.

quests.hint: Having the opposite of the intended effect.
quests.explanation: 'Counterproductive' means producing the opposite of what you wanted.
quests.textToSpeak: Working through the night is often ___; you make more mistakes and end up slower.
quests.correctAnswer: Working through the night is often counterproductive; you make more mistakes and end up slower.
quests.contextClue: Extra effort produces worse results.

quests.hint: Having more than one possible meaning.
quests.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation. The noun is 'ambiguity'.
quests.textToSpeak: The instructions were so ___ that three of us understood them in three different ways.
quests.correctAnswer: The instructions were so ambiguous that three of us understood them in three different ways.
quests.contextClue: Three readers found three meanings.

quests.hint: An agreement where each side gives something up.
quests.explanation: A 'compromise' is an agreement in which both sides make concessions. It is also a verb: 'compromise on price'.
quests.textToSpeak: Neither side got everything it wanted, so the final deal was a ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Neither side got everything it wanted, so the final deal was a compromise.
quests.contextClue: Both sides were only partly satisfied.
